title: Optically Active Single Hole Spin in ZnSe
authors: Amirehsan Alizadehherfati, Yuxi Jiang, Kelsey J. Mirrielees, Nils von den Driesch, Christine Falter, Yurii Kutovyi, Amirehsan Boreiri, Douglas L. Irving, Alexander Pawlis, Edo Waks
abstract: Semiconductor hole spins offer a pathway to extended coherence times by decoupling from nuclear magnetic noise, while their spin-orbit coupling enables fast all-electrical control. In ZnSe, however, realizing this potential has been limited by p-doping challenges. Here, we circumvent this limit by optically activating acceptors within the ZnSe quantum well. We isolate a single-hole spin bound to a shallow acceptor, confirmed by antibunching and accessed via the fast (244 ps) radiative recombination of a bound exciton. Magnetic and Raman spectroscopy of the ground state reveal an effective hole g-factor of 0.7 and an optical resonance linewidth of 26.7 GHz. Complementary first-principles simulations, together with the experimental results, provide evidence that points toward nitrogen as the most likely acceptor impurity. These results introduce a promising new platform for optically active spin qubits and single-photon sources in ZnSe.
summary: The authors report on the successful creation and characterization of optically active single hole spins in ZnSe quantum wells by using an acceptor impurity instead of traditional p-doping. They confirm single-photon emission via antibunching and model the spin dynamics using rate equations derived from optical measurements. This establishes a viable solid-state platform for developing semiconductor-based quantum information devices.
main_problem: The research aims to realize optically active single hole spins in ZnSe, overcoming limitations associated with conventional p-doping methods.
main_result: They successfully isolated a single-hole spin bound to an acceptor impurity and demonstrated its optical activity, establishing a promising platform for spin qubits and single-photon sources.
method: The study combines first-principles DFT calculations to predict defect levels with advanced optical measurements like time-resolved photoluminescence, photon autocorrelation ($	ext{g}^{(2)}(	au)$), and magnetospectroscopy.
model_or_system: The physical system is a single-hole spin bound to a shallow acceptor impurity (likely Nitrogen) within a ZnSe quantum well heterostructure. The dynamics are modeled using rate equations describing transitions between ionized, neutral, and exciton states.
key_observables: Effective hole g-factor ($\approx 0.7$), optical resonance linewidth ($26.7 	ext{ GHz}$), fast radiative lifetime ($\sim 244 	ext{ ps}$), and antibunching in $	ext{g}^{(2)}(0)$.
important_parameters: Acceptor ionization energy ($	ext{E}_{	ext{A}}$) and the relative rates of optical excitation, resonant pumping, and charge trapping.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that optically activating acceptors circumvents p-doping challenges; a limitation noted is that coherence remains limited by spectral diffusion from fluctuating charge environments.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison of impurity formation energies (DFT), PL spectra showing bound excitons, power dependence confirming two-level saturation, time decay curves, and $	ext{g}^{(2)}(	au)$ plots demonstrating antibunching.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the physical challenge (p-doping limitations) to proposing an optical activation mechanism. It details spectroscopic characterization (g-factor, linewidth), confirms single-photon emission ($	ext{g}^{(2)}$), and models the population dynamics using rate equations based on varying excitation powers.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses solid-state quantum memory and spin qubits by demonstrating electrical control over hole spins via optical pumping in a semiconductor material. The combination of DFT modeling with time-domain spectroscopy is highly relevant to open quantum systems research.
